## Discovery & Translational Science

* **[Anti-seizure drug levetiracetam targets diffuse midline glioma](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04646-6)** — *Nature Medicine*
  * Levetiracetam selectively dampens GABAergic synaptic signaling, leading to reduced tumor growth and prolonged survival in experimental models and patient cohorts of diffuse midline glioma.
  * This therapeutic effect is specific to midline gliomas (not hemispheric high-grade gliomas) and operates independently of the drug's canonical SV2A-mediated primary anti-seizure mechanism.

* **[Manganese availability regulates Akt activity and insulin sensitivity](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.02.746017)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * Hepatocyte manganese (Mn) concentrations act as a key determinant of PI3K-independent Akt function in vivo, with Mn levels fluctuating during fasting and feeding via the transporter SLC30A10.
  * Mn increases Akt's catalytic efficiency, acting additively with insulin to enhance Akt activity and suppress hepatic glucose output.

* **[Scn9a inhibition protects pancreatic beta cells in type 1 diabetes](https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.06.11.544521)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * Pharmacological or genetic knockout of the Na⁺ channel β-subunit gene *Scn9a* (Nav1.7) in NOD mice significantly reduced β-cell Na⁺ currents, Ca²⁺ responses, and insulin secretion under high-glucose conditions.
  * The sodium channel inhibitor carbamazepine protects human and mouse β-cell survival in vitro and in vivo, and its protective pathway is mediated through *Scn9a*.

* **[Large-scale oncology pharmacogenomics platform maps systemic toxicity determinants](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363259)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * Researchers developed MSK-Tox, an LLM-based pan-cancer resource capturing clinical toxicity events (pneumonitis, liver toxicity, colitis, etc.) across more than 50,000 patients.
  * The analysis identified a germline regulatory variant near *FOXE1* that confers a high risk of thyroid toxicity across multiple systemic therapy regimens.

* **[Genetic variant drives 25-fold higher lung cancer risk in never-smokers](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/rare-gene-variant-boosts-lung-cancer-risk-25-fold-in-non-smokers/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT News*
  * A newly identified, highly rare genetic variant has been associated with a 25-fold increase in the odds of developing lung cancer among individuals who have never smoked.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **[Biotech]** **[Allogene's off-the-shelf CAR-T receives FDA RMAT designation](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/latest-car-t-good-and-bad)** — *Science.org*
  * Allogene Therapeutics received "Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy" (RMAT) designation for its allogeneic CAR-T pipeline.
  * The designation follows encouraging interim efficacy and safety data readouts at the enrollment of the 24th patient in an ongoing clinical trial aiming to delay relapse in pretreated lymphoma patients.

* **[Biotech]** **[Laromestrocel stem cell therapy preserves brain volume in mild Alzheimer's](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363132)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * A Phase I/II trial (N=49) of the mesenchymal stem cell therapy laromestrocel in mild Alzheimer's disease demonstrated significant inhibition of progressive brain inflammation.
  * Compared to placebo (N=9), subjects receiving monthly doses of 25 million (25M) or 100 million (100M) cells over 39 weeks showed reduced neuroinflammation in the left hippocampus (p < 0.001) and reduced plasma neurogranin (p = 0.023).
  * Decreased neuroinflammation correlated directly with reduced brain atrophy (R = -0.326, p = 0.040) and improved MoCA cognitive scores (R = -0.401, p = 0.011).

* **[Closed-loop auditory stimulation during sleep improves memory in early Alzheimer's](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.14.26360893)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial (N=37) in patients with biomarker-confirmed early symptomatic Alzheimer's tested one night of closed-loop auditory stimulation (CLAS) of slow sleep oscillations.
  * CLAS significantly improved overnight declarative memory retention (word-pair consolidation, Cohen's dz = 0.42, p = 0.04) and enhanced slow-wave and fast spindle electrophysiological activity.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Compounded microdose tirzepatide achieves clinical weight loss](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.15.26363172)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * A retrospective observational study analyzed 93 clinical measurements from obese adults (BMI ≥27) initiating compounded tirzepatide at microdoses of 1 mg or 2 mg weekly—substantially lower than the standard 2.5 mg/week starting dose.
  * Patients demonstrated significant weight reductions within 14–89 days of treatment exposure before undergoing any dose escalation.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Eisai dose-expansion trial reports eribulin liposome activity in breast cancer](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42754887/)** — *PubMed*
  * The Phase I dose-expansion portion of Study 114 evaluated E7389-LF (liposomal eribulin formulation) as a first-line chemotherapy.
  * The study showed manageable safety and early efficacy signals in patients with metastatic or advanced HER2-negative breast cancer.

* **[Biotech]** **[MacroGenics lists first-in-human trial for MGC030](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2100578796462088438)** — *Jacob Plieth*
  * A first-in-human trial for MGC030 has been posted.
  * MGC030 is described as a topoisomerase I inhibitor antibody-drug conjugate (topo1i ADC); specific target details remain unannounced.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Pembrolizumab combination extends survival in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01205-5/fulltext?rss=yes)** — *The Lancet*
  * Data from the Phase III ENGOT-ov65/KEYNOTE-B96 trial show that pembrolizumab plus weekly paclitaxel, with or without bevacizumab, is highly active in patients with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer who received ≤2 prior lines of therapy.
  * The regimen demonstrated clinically significant improvements in progression-free survival (PFS) and clinically meaningful gains in overall survival (OS) in a historically poor-prognosis setting.

* **[GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation is associated with 60% excess muscle loss](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.15.26363157)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * A prospective, population-based MRI study matched 58 adults with diabetes initiating GLP-1 RAs against 130 unexposed controls over 4.6 years.
  * GLP-1 RA initiators experienced 2.75 percentage points more skeletal muscle volume loss (95% CI -4.51 to -0.99; p = 0.003) and 2.54 percentage points greater weight loss (p = 0.021) than controls.
  * Skeletal muscle volume decreased by roughly 60% more in the GLP-1 RA cohort, while differences in adipose tissue reductions (internal torso and subcutaneous) were statistically non-significant.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Tirzepatide and dulaglutide exit interviews in SURPASS-CVOT](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42754765/)** — *PubMed*
  * Exit interviews within the SURPASS-CVOT trial examined patient-reported experiences with tirzepatide and dulaglutide, providing qualitative insights into tolerability, patient burden, and treatment satisfaction.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Long-term pediatric safety of teduglutide in short bowel syndrome](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42754721/)** — *PubMed*
  * A multicenter post-marketing cohort study confirmed the safety and long-term effectiveness of teduglutide (Takeda's Gattex) in pediatric patients with intestinal failure due to short bowel syndrome.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Biotech]** **[FDA approves Ultragenyx's Fayuvi as first gene therapy for Sanfilippo syndrome Type A](http://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-gene-therapy-pediatric-patients-sanfilippo-syndrome-type)** — *FDA* / *[STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/sanfilippo-syndrome-treatment-ultragenyx-approval/?utm_campaign=rss)*
  * The FDA approved Fayuvi (rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf) for the treatment of pediatric patients with mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA / Sanfilippo syndrome type A).
  * Fayuvi represents the first disease-modifying treatment approved for this rare, progressive, and fatal pediatric neurodegenerative disease.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[FDA issues safety updates on Prolia and GLP-1 RAs](http://www.fda.gov/about-fda/center-drug-evaluation-and-research-cder/drug-safety-oversight-board-dsb-meeting-june-26-2024)** — *FDA*
  * The FDA added a Boxed Warning to Amgen's Prolia (denosumab) highlighting a high risk of severe hypocalcemia in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease.
  * Separately, a preliminary FDA Drug Safety Board evaluation did not find evidence linking GLP-1 receptor agonists to an increased risk of suicidal thoughts or actions.

* **[Big Pharma] [Biotech]** **[FDA Office of Prescription Drug Promotion issues multiple untitled letters](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/warning-letters-and-notice-violation-letters-pharmaceutical-companies/untitled-letters)** — *FDA*
  * The FDA's OPDP issued four promotional untitled letters over marketing violations:
    * **[Biotech]** Alar Pharmaceuticals for ALA-3000 (ketamine pamoate) injection (August 2026).
    * **[Biotech]** Travere Therapeutics for Filspari (sparsentan) tablets (July 2026).
    * **[Big Pharma]** Sanofi Vaccines for Beyfortus (nirsevimab-alip) injection (July 2026).
    * **[Big Pharma]** Viatris Specialty for Tobi Podhaler (tobramycin inhalation powder) (July 2026).

* **[Target trial emulation framework proposed for proactive Medicare pharmacovigilance](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.01.26356874)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * A study using Medicare fee-for-service claims (2017–2019) developed an active pharmacovigilance framework by emulating sequential daily target trials to detect adverse drug event signals in older adults initiating atorvastatin post-infarction.

* **[FDA hiring delays persist due to bureaucratic bottlenecks and DOGE cuts](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/fda-hiring-bottleneck-senate-hearings-chris-klomp-nicole-saphier/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT News*
  * Despite promises of a post-budget cut hiring wave, the FDA is stymied by administrative delays and the lingering effects of last year's Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) cuts.

## Business & Strategy

* **[Biotech]** **[Electra Therapeutics prices $350M upsized IPO for registrational trials](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/electra-biotech-ipo-price-secondary-hlh/830698/)** — *BioPharma Dive* / *[BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2100749907090956731)*
  * Electra Therapeutics priced an upsized $350 million initial public offering at $15 per share to fund development of its lead candidate, ipsoprubart, an experimental drug targeting secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH).
  * Ipsoprubart is currently in a registrational trial, with enrollment expected to complete in the second half of 2027.

* **[Big Pharma]** **[Novo Nordisk partners with Orbis Medicines in $1.4B oral macrocycle deal](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novo-orbis-macrocyclic-peptides-oral-obesity-drugs/830645/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  * Novo Nordisk signed a discovery and development collaboration with Orbis Medicines to identify oral macrocycle therapeutics against multiple cardiometabolic targets.
  * Orbis is eligible for up to $1.4 billion in upfront, milestone, and downstream payments. The macrocycle approach is designed to overcome low gastrointestinal absorption rates typical of standard oral peptides.

* **[Biotech]** **[North Immunology merges with Aethlon Medical in Dupixent-competitor play](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/north-immunology-aethlon-biotech-reverse-merger-eczema-drug/830631/)** — *BioPharma Dive*
  * North Immunology announced a reverse merger with Aethlon Medical to go public on the Nasdaq under the ticker NRTX in Q1 2027, with North's shareholders owning 95.25% of the combined entity.
  * The transaction will advance North's early-stage development program targeting inflammatory skin diseases, aiming to compete with Sanofi's Dupixent.

* **[Biotech]** **[Economic analysis evaluates value of $39.8K/month pancreatic cancer drug daraxonrasib](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363246)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * An economic evaluation using a 3-state partitioned survival model assessed the cost-effectiveness of daraxonrasib—the first approved broad RAS-targeted drug—against chemotherapy.
  * While daraxonrasib doubled overall survival in the RAS G12-mutant population in the Phase III RASolute 302 trial, its US wholesale acquisition cost (WAC) of $39,800 per 30-day supply challenges conventional cost-effectiveness benchmarks.

## Public Health & Policy

* **[HHS Secretary Kennedy launches autism research fund and USPSTF overhaul](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/17/kennedy-announces-new-research-fund-to-improve-autism-diagnoses/?utm_campaign=rss)** — *STAT News*
  * Health Secretary RFK Jr. announced a new federal research fund to modernize autism diagnoses, while reviving the dormant USPSTF preventive services panel by appointing eight new members.
  * Kennedy also used a keynote at the Children's Health Defense conference to reiterate his criticisms of standard vaccination protocols.

* **[Mpox Clade IIb persistence sustained by high-risk sexual networks](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363229)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * An epidemiological agent-based model of Mpox Clade IIb transmission in Berlin demonstrated that behavioral changes and vaccines successfully reduced initial case numbers, but localized contact densities within high-risk MSM networks sustained endemic, low-level transmission.

* **[Emergency presentations drive survival inequities in ovarian cancer](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01543-6/fulltext?rss=yes)** — *The Lancet*
  * Lancet Commission correspondence highlights that up to 50% of ovarian cancer patients in some regions are diagnosed via emergency department presentations.
  * These emergency-presenting patients are more likely to be older and frail, and they are routinely excluded from optimized diagnostic pathways, surgical intervention, and novel therapeutics.

* **[Wastewater surveillance shows high utility for highly-shed pathogen outbreaks](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.16.26363050)** — *bioRxiv/medRxiv*
  * Modeling of viral shedding patterns showed that wastewater surveillance is most effective for emerging pathogens shedding 10× to 100× more than SARS-CoV-2 (e.g., Influenza A, Lassa, and Ebola).

***

**Worth watching:** The prospective population-based finding that GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation is associated with ~60% excess skeletal muscle volume loss over matched controls could pivot drug pipelines further toward combination treatments pairing incretins with muscle-preserving agents.

- Biology & Health
    - [Supplementing Serine to fix Stress and Insulin Resistance!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xEHCe1MMgc) -- Physionic
        - Examines the physiological link between acute psychological stress, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), elevated blood glucose, and the development of type 2 diabetes.
        - Details research on how senescence in amygdala astrocytes drives stress-induced anxiety and hyperglycemia in biological models.
        - Explores therapeutic applications and clinical trials investigating D-serine supplementation to mitigate stress responses and associated metabolic disruption.
    - [What Happens When AI Bots Fight Over Medical Codes?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/vhOGTqICwH8) -- Health2Tech
        - Features Ashley Cairns discussing potential conflicts when competing AI bots interact over medical coding and levels of care.
        - Addresses the operational impact of automated payer and provider AI tools clashing during revenue cycle management.
        - Examines how AI-driven coding disputes could restructure healthcare reimbursement dynamics and clinical documentation processes.
    - [Beyond AI Chatbots: Building the Infrastructure Healthcare Actually Needs with Ashley Cairns](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qOQIcEeRMGE) -- Health2Tech
        - Features Keywell.ai Founder & CEO Ashley Cairns explaining the need for HIPAA-compliant "AI scaffolding" infrastructure to automate complex healthcare workflows without vendor lock-in.
        - Explores the dynamics between health plans and healthcare providers in adopting AI for prior authorization, claims appeals, and medical coding.
        - Recommends deploying multiple foundation models instead of a single LLM to safely manage model replacements in production environments.
        - Stresses that healthcare organizations must evaluate AI performance using their own real-world data rather than relying on public benchmarks.
- Pure Science
    - [Why Navier-Stokes Pushes Math and Physics to the Edge](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PsWR1rQEWYo) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Explores fluid dynamics and the $1 million Millennium Prize Problem regarding whether solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations always remain smooth or develop finite-time blowups.
        - Explains the mathematical derivation of fluid mechanics from the inviscid Euler equations to the addition of the viscosity term.
        - Outlines historical progress on partial differential equations and blowup conditions, highlighting work by Jean Leray, Terence Tao, Córdoba, and Martínez-Zoroa.
        - Details recent mathematical advances, including proof of Euler blowup by Buckmaster and Alpöge alongside a novel OpenAI proof demonstrating blowup in Navier-Stokes equations.
- Other
    - [Crash Course Astronomy Marathon • Full Series](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HICDzXfCAs4) -- CrashCourse
        - Compiles a 46-episode series covering foundational observational astronomy, celestial mechanics, lunar cycles, and gravitational dynamics.
        - Surveys the composition, structure, and dynamics of the Solar System, detailing planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and the Oort Cloud.
        - Explains stellar astrophysics, including stellar evolution, white dwarfs, high-mass stellar collapse, neutron stars, and black holes.
        - Covers extragalactic astronomy, active galactic nuclei, dark matter, cosmological models of the Big Bang, and deep time.
